title: Systems operating in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces have minimal consciousness

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Systems operating in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces have minimal consciousness

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: TAME provisionally holds that consciousness comes in degrees and that embodiment includes perception-action systems in any space, implying that systems operating in morphogenetic, transcriptional and other spaces should have some, if very minimal, degree of consciousness.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Consciousness

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This implies, counter to many people’s intuitions, that systems that operate in morphogenetic, transcriptional, and other spaces should also have some (if very minimal) degree of consciousness.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Consciousness”. Scope: Tissues, cell collectives and other non-neural systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-31: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.04

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim concerns phenomenal consciousness, not merely adaptive behavior or information processing. Existing biological data cannot decide between conscious and non-conscious descriptions of identical dynamics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No current observation distinguishes a morphogenetic or transcriptional system with minimal phenomenal consciousness from a functionally identical system without it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Minimal consciousness in non-reporting systems has no agreed empirical marker.

The inference follows from TAME's provisional premises rather than a discriminating test.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.02
analysis feasibility: 0.08
data existence: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.05
discriminating power: 0.02

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement infers a minimal degree of consciousness for systems whose perception and action are in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces. Regulation, goal-like setpoints, and transcriptional change are measurable, and those measurements are exactly what a non-conscious account of the same systems also predicts. No existing dataset draws the distinction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No public measurement would be positive if a morphogenetic or transcriptional system had a minimal degree of consciousness and negative if it only regulated those variables.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Degree of consciousness, as first-person experience, is not separated by any dataset from competent regulation in the same state space.
